mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) as a continuous variable predicts positive 20-day forward S&P 500 returns, as lower rates reduce the discount rate for equity valuation and increase liquidity in financial markets.
failure_condition: Rank IC between FEDFUNDS and 20d forward returns is <= 0.03 in any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the CPIAUCSL (Consumer Price Index) of more than 0.3% signals rising inflation, which triggers a sell-off in equities and predicts negative 20-day forward S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: In periods where CPIAUCSL monthly change exceeds 0.3%, the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous weakening in the GDP (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) signals a deteriorating economic demand, which predicts negative 20-day forward S&P 500 returns as investors anticipate a recession.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both below 3-month moving average
failure_condition: The interaction term (GDPC1 and HOUST both below 3-month moving average) fails to predict negative returns: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: In monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS > 2.0% and rising), the S&P 500 experiences negative 20-day forward returns due to increased cost of capital and reduced liquidity.
failure_condition: In periods where FEDFUNDS > 2.0% and rising, the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) as a continuous variable predicts negative 60-day forward S&P 500 returns, as falling industrial output signals weakening economic activity and reduced corporate earnings.
failure_condition: Rank IC between INDPRO and 60d forward returns is positive or <= 0.03 in any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 5.0% signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which predicts negative 5-day forward S&P 500 returns due to reduced consumer spending and corporate profit pressures.
failure_condition: In periods where UNRATE > 5.0%, the 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous deterioration in unemployment rate (UNRATE) and labor force participation (PAYEMS) signals a weakening labor market, which predicts negative 20-day forward S&P 500 returns as consumer spending and corporate hiring decline.
failure_condition: The interaction term (UNRATE > 4.5% and PAYEMS < 3-month moving average) fails to predict negative returns: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 1200.0 thousand units signals a weakening housing market, which predicts negative 20-day forward S&P 500 returns due to reduced consumer confidence and economic activity.
failure_condition: In periods where HOUST < 1200.0, the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of cases.
